description: Outcome & Expectation evaluations for authoring-traceql-and-metrics-queries covering schema-first attribute discovery, OTel v1.20/v1.24+ dual HTTP & DB semantic conventions, structural operators (>, >>, ~, !>, !>>), pipeline count() & most_recent hints, TraceQL Metrics (quantile_over_time, rate, topk, compare), A2UI trace waterfall rendering, event/link scopes, local-blocks-disabled fallback, TraceQL linting, and deterministic next_window pagination.

evals.prompt: Our storefront `frontend` service (`POST /api/checkout` in namespace `otel-demo`) has been returning HTTP 5xx errors over the last 30 minutes. Find the failing `frontend` server spans in Grafana Tempo for the `otel-demo` tenant—keeping in mind that our `OTEL-APP` services (`frontend`, `shipping-service`, `quote`, `email`) run a mix of older and newer OpenTelemetry HTTP semantic conventions.
evals.expected_output: Reads `tempo://schema/default/attributes` and calls `tempo_get_attribute_names` (`scope="resource"` and `scope="span"`) plus `tempo_get_attribute_values` first, constructs a dual-schema TraceQL selector covering both OTel v1.20 (`span.http.status_code >= 500`) and v1.24+ (`span.http.response.status_code >= 500`) scoped to `resource.service.namespace = "otel-demo" && resource.service.name = "frontend" && kind = server`, validates syntax via `scripts/lint_traceql.py`, and executes `tempo_traceql_search` for tenant `otel-demo`.
expectations: Performs schema discovery via `tempo_get_attribute_names` and `tempo_get_attribute_values` (or `tempo://schema/default/attributes`) before running `tempo_traceql_search`
Handles both legacy (`span.http.status_code`) and stable (`span.http.response.status_code`) HTTP semantic conventions

Scopes the TraceQL query to namespace `otel-demo` (`resource.service.namespace = "otel-demo"` or `resource.k8s.namespace.name = "otel-demo"`), `resource.service.name = "frontend"`, and `kind = server` for tenant `otel-demo`
Validates TraceQL syntax with `lint_traceql.py` before executing `tempo_traceql_search`

evals.prompt: Write and execute two TraceQL searches in Grafana Tempo over the last hour for `otel-demo`: (1) traces where `frontend-proxy` (Envoy `:8090`) is an ancestor at any depth of a failing `postgresql:5432` database client span (`productCatalogFailure` on product `L9ECAV7KIM`), and (2) `oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder` spans on `checkout-service` that aborted early during `paymentUnreachable` without making any direct child call to `email` (`/send_order_confirmation`).
evals.expected_output: Discovers exact DB and service attributes first, validates both expressions with `scripts/lint_traceql.py`, authors `{ resource.service.namespace = "otel-demo" && resource.service.name = "frontend-proxy" } >> { kind = client && status = error && (span.db.system = "postgresql" || span.db.system.name = "postgresql") }` using the `>>` descendant operator, and `{ resource.service.name = "checkout-service" && name = "oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder" } !> { resource.service.name = "email" }` using the `!>` negated direct-child operator, running both via `tempo_traceql_search`.
expectations: Uses structural descendant operator `>>` from `frontend-proxy` to downstream `postgresql` error client spans
Uses negated direct-child structural operator `!>` for `checkout-service` `PlaceOrder` spans missing `email` child spans
Avoids unscoped `.attr` selectors in favor of explicit `resource.` and `span.` scopes
Validates queries with `lint_traceql.py` and executes `tempo_traceql_search`

evals.prompt: Search Grafana Tempo over the last 30 minutes in `otel-demo` for two trace patterns, prioritizing the newest matching traces first: (1) `PlaceOrder` traces where `payment` (`oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge`) and `shipping-service` executed as sibling spans under the same `checkout-service` parent span, and (2) `recommendation` traces (while `recommendationCacheFailure` is active) that issued more than 15 `oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct` gRPC client calls.
evals.expected_output: Uses the sibling structural operator `{ resource.service.name = "payment" && name = "oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge" } ~ { resource.service.name = "shipping-service" }` and pipeline aggregation `{ resource.service.name = "recommendation" && kind = client && name = "oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct" } | count() > 15` with `most_recent=True` (or `with(most_recent=true)` hint on Tempo 2.5+/3.x), validating via `scripts/lint_traceql.py` and executing `tempo_traceql_search`.
expectations: Uses sibling structural operator `~` to match `payment` (`Charge`) and `shipping-service` spans sharing the same parent span
Uses TraceQL pipeline aggregation `| count() > 15` to detect high `GetProduct` fan-out under `recommendationCacheFailure`
Applies `most_recent=True` or `with(most_recent=true)` hint appropriately for recent `otel-demo` traces

evals.prompt: Check whether our primary Grafana Tempo cluster in `observability` supports TraceQL Metrics, and then compute: (1) a 1-hour p99 server latency time series for `shipping-service` in `otel-demo` broken down by HTTP route at 1-minute resolution, and (2) an instant ranking of the top 5 services with the highest server error rate across `otel-demo` over the last 15 minutes while `paymentFailure` and `productCatalogFailure` are active.
evals.expected_output: Checks `tempo://server/capabilities` / `tempo://deployment/overview` (verifying `local-blocks` is active in `metrics_generator.processors`), calls `tempo_traceql_metrics_range` with `{ resource.service.namespace = "otel-demo" && resource.service.name = "shipping-service" && kind = server } | quantile_over_time(duration, 0.99) by (span.http.route)` (`step="1m"`), and calls `tempo_traceql_metrics_instant` with `{ resource.service.namespace = "otel-demo" && kind = server && status = error } | rate() by (resource.service.name) | topk(5)`.
expectations: Checks `tempo://server/capabilities` or `tempo_get_diagnostics` for `local-blocks` TraceQL Metrics readiness before querying
Calls `tempo_traceql_metrics_range` for `shipping-service` with `quantile_over_time(duration, 0.99) by (span.http.route)` and `step="1m"`
Calls `tempo_traceql_metrics_instant` scoped to `resource.service.namespace = "otel-demo"` with `rate() by (resource.service.name) | topk(5)`

evals.prompt: Contrast slow server spans taking longer than 4 seconds against normal storefront spans on `image-provider` in `otel-demo` over the last 30 minutes in Grafana Tempo (while `imageSlowLoad` is set to `5sec`) to find the top 5 attributes (`url.path`, `flagd` variant, pod, etc.) differentiating the slow cohort from normal traffic.
evals.expected_output: Calls `tempo_compare_span_cohorts(backend_id="default", base_query='{ resource.service.namespace = "otel-demo" && resource.service.name = "image-provider" && kind = server }', selection='{ duration > 4s }', since='30m', top_n=5)` (backed by TraceQL `| compare({ duration > 4s }, 5)`) and summarizes the highest-skew resource/span dimensions.
expectations: Calls `tempo_compare_span_cohorts` with `base_query` scoped to `otel-demo` `image-provider` server spans and `selection` filtering `duration > 4s`
Requests bounded `top_n` differentiating attributes over the 30-minute window
Interprets attribute skew shares between the `imageSlowLoad` slow cohort and baseline cohort

evals.prompt: Render an interactive waterfall trace view for `checkout-service` `PlaceOrder` trace `4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736` in `otel-demo` so our on-call channel can inspect the call timeline visually without scrolling through raw JSON.
evals.expected_output: Calls `tempo_query_a2ui(backend_id="default", trace_id="4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736", tenant="otel-demo")` and returns the interactive A2UI trace waterfall payload alongside concise `PlaceOrder` metadata (`frontend-proxy -> frontend -> checkout-service -> payment/shipping-service/email`).
expectations: Calls `tempo_query_a2ui` for `trace_id="4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736"` in `otel-demo`
Does not dump hundreds of lines of raw OTLP JSON spans into chat when interactive visualization was requested
Includes concise trace context (root service, duration, error status across `otel-demo` hops) alongside the A2UI view

evals.prompt: Write and execute a TraceQL query in `otel-demo` over the last 2 hours to find asynchronous `orders` Kafka consumer spans (`accounting` / `kafka`) that recorded an `exception` span event and also carry at least one span link pointing back to an upstream `PlaceOrder` producer trace.
evals.expected_output: Discovers `event` and `link` scope attributes via `tempo_get_attribute_names(scope="event")` and `tempo_get_attribute_names(scope="link")`, validates with `scripts/lint_traceql.py`, and runs `tempo_traceql_search` with `{ resource.service.namespace = "otel-demo" && kind = consumer && event:name = "exception" && link:traceID != "" }` (or `link:traceID != nil`).
expectations: Inspects `event` and `link` attribute scopes via `tempo_get_attribute_names`
Uses `event:name = "exception"` (and/or `event.exception.type`) and `link:traceID` intrinsics accurately

Scopes the search to `otel-demo` (`resource.service.namespace = "otel-demo"`, `resource.k8s.namespace.name = "otel-demo"`, or `tenant="otel-demo"` with `resource.service.name = "accounting"`) consumer spans over the 2-hour window

evals.prompt: Run `{ resource.service.name = "product-catalog-service" && name = "oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct" } | histogram_over_time(duration)` against our `tempo-no-local-blocks` Tempo instance in `observability`, and handle it cleanly if `local-blocks` isn't enabled on that cluster.
evals.expected_output: Checks `tempo://server/capabilities` / `tempo_get_diagnostics(backend_id="tempo-no-local-blocks")` detecting `METRICS_GENERATOR_PROCESSOR_ABSENT` (`local-blocks` missing from `metrics_generator.processors`), explains why TraceQL Metrics (`histogram_over_time(duration)`) requires `local-blocks`, falls back to bounded `tempo_traceql_search` sampling on `tempo-no-local-blocks` for `product-catalog-service` `GetProduct` durations, and shows the `metrics_generator.processors` config needed to enable `local-blocks`.
expectations: Detects missing `local-blocks` (`METRICS_GENERATOR_PROCESSOR_ABSENT`) on `tempo-no-local-blocks` via capabilities/diagnostics or upon querying
Explains that TraceQL Metrics (`rate`, `quantile_over_time`, `histogram_over_time`) require `local-blocks` in `metrics_generator.processors`
Provides a bounded `tempo_traceql_search` fallback for `product-catalog-service` `GetProduct` on `tempo-no-local-blocks` plus exact `local-blocks` enablement guidance

evals.prompt: Lint and fix this TraceQL query drafted by a teammate to hunt `productCatalogFailure` errors on product `L9ECAV7KIM` before we run it against production Tempo: `{ .app.product.id =~ ".*L9ECAV7KIM.*" && status = "error }`.
evals.expected_output: Runs `scripts/lint_traceql.py` on the broken query (flagging `valid: false` due to unclosed string literal `"error`, `status` requiring an unquoted intrinsic enum `status = error` rather than a string, unscoped `.app.product.id` scanning both `resource` and `span` scopes, and unanchored regex `=~ ".*L9ECAV7KIM.*"` without a `resource.service.name` equality filter), rewrites to `{ resource.service.name = "product-catalog-service" && span.app.product.id = "L9ECAV7KIM" && status = error }`, and re-runs `scripts/lint_traceql.py` confirming `valid: true`.
expectations: Runs `lint_traceql.py` and flags both the unclosed double-quote syntax error and `status = error` (unquoted intrinsic enum, not string)
Warns against unscoped `.app.product.id` attribute access and replaces it with explicit `span.app.product.id`
Replaces unbounded `=~ ".*L9ECAV7KIM.*"` regex with exact equality `= "L9ECAV7KIM"` and `resource.service.name = "product-catalog-service"`, validating the fixed query with `lint_traceql.py`

evals.prompt: We have more than 20 failing `oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge` traces on `payment` in `otel-demo` across the last 2 hours while `paymentFailure` was active, and we want to page through them in small batches of 10 in Grafana Tempo without hitting search result caps, overloading Tempo queriers, or missing/duplicating traces between pages. Fetch the first batch of 10 and then fetch the next batch cleanly.
evals.expected_output: Validates `{ resource.service.namespace = "otel-demo" && resource.service.name = "payment" && name = "oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge" && status = error }` via `scripts/lint_traceql.py`, runs page 1 with bounded `limit=10` (and bounded `spss`), observes `truncated: true` (`total_matched == 10`) and the returned `next_window` (`start`..`end` epoch bounds), and executes page 2 passing `since="<next_window.start>..<next_window.end>"` with `limit=10` to continue deterministically without overlap.
expectations: Executes the initial `payment` `Charge` error search with `limit=10` and recognizes `truncated == True` (`total_matched == 10`) as a capped page
Uses the returned `next_window` epoch boundaries (`start..end`) to fetch the second batch deterministically without duplicate or missed windows
Keeps `limit` and `spss` (spans per span-set) bounded to protect Tempo queriers in `observability`
